correctness.rationale: The maximal-ideal cotangent map is invertible. Pairwise-zero products force every long-branch row of its matrix to have at most one nonzero coefficient, while a short generator x_i^2=0 prohibits any long linear component; the block matrix has invertible GL_r short block and long monomial block. A long generator has a unique principal branch; power relations force an exponent-preserving permutation. The annihilator of x_j times a unit in k[x_j]/(x_j^{d_j}) is exactly k x_j^{d_j-1}; every off-principal component is therefore a socle scalar. Conversely the normal form respects all products/powers and invertible cotangent map implies automorphism by Nakayama. Counting free parameters over F_q yields |GL_r(q)| * product_e m_e! * (q-1)^s * q^(rs+s(n-1)+sum_{long}(d_i-2)); special all-short, all-long and n=1 boundaries are consistent.
